It can't only be an issue with the new drivers, there should be logic that throttles and then shuts down the GPU if it overheats.

The internal logic is to throttle the GPU and memory clocks, first turning off the boost clock then dropping down to the idle clocks all while automatically increasing fan speed. The problem seems to come from the fact the driver software can overwrite / disable this, someone failed to make doubly sure the variable in control of the fan speeds is actually being reset to its proper state.

The fan controller should be independent and fully controllable by the driver. But the fail-safe that shuts down the GPU to prevent damage in case of overheating (e.g. due to fan failure) should never be. That would be unacceptable. Remember, Intel designed P4 CPUs that even survived a complete removal of the HSF. Simple fan failures happen all the time. It could be that some other component such as the VRMs failed though.

A VRM failure wouldn't cause this, thermal shut offs are built into virtually every voltage regulator you can buy today. If you hit that point where it can't regulate voltage then a MOV (metal oxide varistor) should be in place to break the circuit, if some cheeky board partner (or AMD) decided to omit protection circuitry like this then yeah a VRM failure might have happened.

All comes down to the fact silicon is never perfect, one stray triboelectric charge produced though the automated movements during assembly and the extremely delicate silicon could have a imperfection that never shows up until late into production (if at all), bring a little heat into the mix and that piece of silicon draws a bit more current maybe too much current and burns itself to death. https://i.imgur.com/5jwXJc7.jpg
